Hi Jennifer — following up with concrete recommendations and short rationale. I'll summarize first, then add practical configs and the attachable SDK snippet.

Top-line recommendations
- Vector dimension: start POC with 1024 as the default mapping for your current 768 vectors. Move to 1536 only if the POC shows measurable ranking gains (>1.5-2% lift on your eval set) that justify cost. 1024 is a good balance for transformer-based encoders we typically see.
- Normalization: continue normalizing at write/ingest time (unit L2). Redwood's default similarity pipelines assume normalized vectors for cosine equivalence; normalizing at write reduces per-query compute and cache variance.
- Batching & ingest sizing: for a 50K file, prefer streaming ingest with chunked batches of 2,048-8,192 vectors. Default safe batch: 4,096 vectors per request with concurrency limit 4 (so at most ~16k in-flight vectors per worker). We can provide a worker config tuned to your instance sizes.
- Migration approach: two-step POC: (1) cold import sample (10K) to validate mapping + reranker performance; (2) parallel serving with a shadow index for a week to compare A/B on ranking metrics.

Practical notes / sample configs
- Example normalization (Python):
  vectors = np.asarray(raw_vectors, dtype=np.float32)
  norms = np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
  vectors = vectors / np.maximum(norms, 1e-12)

- Suggested ingest request pattern (pseudo):
  POST /v1/embeddings/ingest  (batch_size=4096)
  headers: Authorization: Bearer <INGEST_KEY>
  query: ?index=nova-prod-region-us-west&normalize=false (already normalized)

- Auth & routing: yes — Redwood supports per-key scoping. Create two API keys: ingest key (scoped to write on the Nova index) and query keys (read-only). Route by header x-region: us-west to ensure locality. We will provide a policy template for your ops team.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-auth-sample.py (contains: example of scoped keys, retry/backoff, incremental upload loop). I'll attach embed-mapping-template.xlsx for mapping confirmation.

Cost delta guidance
- Rough delta (illustrative) vs current 768-d floats: moving to 1024 increases storage/compute by ~33%; 1536 increases by ~100% relative to 768. Actual per-query token/compute cost depends on your reranker and approx-nearest-neighbor index config (HNSW vs flat). We'll run a short benchmark during POC and give a per-query $ delta.

Next operational asks from us
1) Share 10K sample + current metadata mapping.
2) Confirm POC start window and preferred test queries / eval set.
3) Which infra flavor for POC: small-GPU pool (g4dn-ish) or larger GPUs? We can size recommendations if you tell us target latency & qps.

Happy to hop on a short call Tue/Wed if you want to walk the team through the sample code.

Jennifer / team — adding a few concrete operational knobs from an ingest perspective:  

- Streaming pattern: read your 50K file line-by-line and emit batches of 4k vectors to the ingest endpoint with a 1s throttle between batch groups (adjustable). This keeps peak memory modest and gives time for the server to free KV cache slots.
- Retry/backoff: use jittered exponential backoff with max attempts = 6. For 413/429 responses, requeue the batch and sleep (base=0.6s, factor=2).
- Checkpointing: persist last-successful-offset in your manifest (we usually write this to S3/Cloud Storage so you can resume).
- Client-side parallelism: 3 concurrent workers per instance for small machines; 8+ for larger instances. Each worker keeps at most 2 batches in-flight to limit GPU memory pressure.

I'll drop a simplified ingest script in the shared Drive and include comments where to swap API keys for read vs write.
